rationale: The workspace VFS resolves a path with a recursive CTE whose join order lets SQLite probe vfs_dirents by parent_inode only (EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN: SEARCH d USING PRIMARY KEY (parent_inode=?)), then filter names through json_each. Every level therefore reads all of a directory's entries and their nodes. With the in-memory resolve cache cold (a new or evicted Durable Object), a path lookup read about 490 rows, so grep -r or the grep tool over 1,000 files read 491,163 rows. CROSS JOIN fixes the order so the probe uses the full (parent_inode, name) key: the same search reads 41,637 rows and glob/find 2,654 instead of 10,175 (measured on a local instance). The query's result is unchanged.
removeWhen: @cloudflare/computer resolves paths with a plan that probes vfs_dirents by (parent_inode, name); tests/vfs-resolve-plan.spec.ts fails on the unpatched query.

rationale: Remove node:fs/promises mkdir calls that are incompatible with Cloudflare Workers. The Edge Computer workspace guarantees /workspace exists. Disable implicit cold-history Agent activation through an optional deployment seam so the Edge single main slot owns activation. The runtime-queues.probe.mjs cold Remote follow plus A-to-B rotation is the failing-without-patch check.
removeWhen: The published session controller routes directory creation through the ctx.fs seam (or gates it behind a platform check). Upstream offers a public way to follow cold history without promoting a resident Agent.

rationale: Resolve the Harness attribution version without runtime node:module path discovery, which is unavailable in the Worker bundle.
removeWhen: The published LLM package exposes its version through a Worker-bundle-safe import or injected build constant and bundles without node:module.

rationale: Parse fetched HTML with the package's Domino dependency before passing a DOM node to Turndown. Wrangler selects Turndown's browser export, whose string parser requires a global document that Cloudflare Workers do not provide, so the unpatched package silently returns raw HTML.
removeWhen: The published tool-web package converts HTML in a Cloudflare Worker without a global document and the Edge web_fetch integration assertions pass without this patch.

rationale: Use the Workers global fetch instead of the Node-only undici import. Reject IP literals and local naming scopes before every request, including each redirect hop. URL checks do not resolve or pin DNS; preserve global_fetch_strictly_public in the Worker configuration for the platform network boundary. Standalone transport tests cover success and redirect rejection; runtime probes cover the deployed transport policy.
removeWhen: The provider exposes a platform-fetch seam without undici, and Edge retains per-hop URL policy and verified platform private-destination restrictions without this patch.

rationale: Defer module-level AbortController construction to first use (`neverAbortedSignal()`); the signal has three use sites since 0.2.1, one of them on the non-owner resource path. Cloudflare Workers disallows new AbortController() in global scope.
removeWhen: The published api-gateway package initializes NEVER_ABORTED_SIGNAL lazily or moves it inside the method that uses it.

rationale: Replace node:fs/promises realpath with lexical path normalization and remove stat calls, both incompatible with Cloudflare Workers. Edge VFS has no symlinks, so lexical resolution of '.', '..', and duplicate separators is exactly realpath's canonical result and keeps caller-supplied traversal paths from persisting alias workspaces.
removeWhen: The published workspace registry accepts an injectable path normalizer or the realpath/stat calls are gated behind a platform check.

rationale: The published bundle inlines dsh-llm's attribution module, which resolves the Harness version with createRequire(import.meta.url)("../package.json") at module load; import.meta.url is undefined in the Worker bundle, so without this patch the Worker fails to start (TypeError from node:module createRequire, reproduced by run-session-integration.mjs). Use the pinned version string, as the dsh-llm patch does.
removeWhen: The published repeat-tool-reminder package imports createUserMessage from @deepseek-ai/dsh-llm instead of inlining it, or the inlined attribution module bundles without node:module.

rationale: The published tools have no target-capability configuration. Restrict model schemas and help to this_session; EdgeSchedule independently rejects automatic Session targets. standalone/tests/schedule-capabilities.test.mjs checks the actual patched bundle and fails without this patch.
removeWhen: Upstream exposes target capabilities through plugin configuration so composition can restrict both validation and help.

rationale: The task editor has no capability seam and manual creation only offers automatic new Session targets. Hide unsupported edit targets and disable that manual entry with guidance to create from a conversation; keep the task list, existing task editor, and chat creation. standalone/tests/schedule-capabilities.test.mjs fails without this patch.
removeWhen: The UI reads supported target capabilities and offers an existing Session picker for manual creation.

rationale: The package default-imports rrule, but the ESM entry selected by Wrangler exports only named values; both Worker builds fail before this patch. Use a namespace import with a CJS default fallback, supporting both the Worker ESM entry and Node-based assembly tests. The build and standalone schedule-capabilities test fail without it.
removeWhen: Upstream util-time uses an import compatible with the published rrule ESM export shape.

rationale: The published model-listing cache schedules background refresh timers when discovery is enabled; these timers prevent a Durable Object from becoming idle even after unref. Remove automatic scheduling while retaining request-driven TTL, stale-while-refresh, credential scoping and single-flight. No public provider option exposes this refresh policy; maxAgeMs=0 also removes caching and can cause request bursts. standalone/tests/model-listing.test.mjs fails without the patch (an idle clock advance performs a second load). This patch alone is not evidence that the complete browser session hibernates.
removeWhen: The published provider exposes a request-driven TTL cache policy that does not schedule background timers, and the Edge idle/reconnect and listing single-flight tests pass without the patch.
